direction_as_read: mixed: older small trials and two pre-2008 meta-analyses favour leaf and flower extract for heart failure symptoms and exercise capacity, while SPICE, the largest trial, and HERB CHF, both add-on to contemporary therapy, were null on their primary outcomes; blood pressure evidence is inconsistent
summary: Stored as positive_strong on one 2003 meta-analysis. A later Cochrane review (18254076) repeats that benefit for symptoms and maximal workload, but both reviews predate SPICE and HERB CHF. SPICE, 2681 patients on WS 1442 900 mg/day for 24 months, had no significant effect on time to first cardiac event (19019730). HERB CHF, 120 patients on 450 mg twice daily, found no difference in 6 minute walk distance and concluded no symptomatic or functional benefit (19789403). Smaller trials report exercise gains, some on liquid fresh-berry extract in drops (12833999, 11715631), and blood pressure results are inconsistent (16762125, 40732315). The two primary-positive fresh-berry trials are liquid extracts in drops, while berry labels here print dry extract, powder or whole berry. Leaf and flower labels print 150 to 500 mg per serving, against the 900 mg/day WS 1442 arms.
